content.title: About
content.content: Unsalted potato chips are thinly sliced potatoes fried or baked until crisp, without any added salt. They retain the natural potato flavor, a slight sweetness, and a crunchy texture. Chips are commonly served as a snack with drinks, in burgers, or as a crunchy topping for salads.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first commercial production of potato chips began in the United States in the mid‑19th century.
Unsalted chips are often chosen by people watching their sodium intake and by athletes who need to control electrolyte balance.
Potato chips can be prepared by deep‑frying or baking; the latter reduces fat content.
There are many flavored versions—barbecue, cheese, sweet‑spicy—but the unsalted version remains the basic product.
Thin slicing ensures an even golden color when cooked at the right temperature.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Chips provide carbohydrates that quickly supply energy, which can be useful before physical activity.

items.title: Contains vitamin C
items.content: A small amount of vitamin C survives proper cooking, supporting the immune system.

items.title: Potassium
items.content: Potatoes are rich in potassium, which helps regulate fluid balance and muscle function.

items.title: Low sodium
items.content: The lack of added salt makes them suitable for low‑sodium diets.

items.title: Convenient snack
items.content: They are easy to pack and eat quickly, making them handy for travel and work.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Even without salt, chips are often fried, which makes them calorie‑dense.

items.title: Acrylamide formation
items.content: Cooking at very high temperatures can produce acrylamides, compounds that may be harmful in large amounts.

items.title: Potato allergy
items.content: Rarely, some individuals may be allergic to potatoes or to the oils used.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: Large portions can cause heaviness due to the high fat content.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Unsalted chips can be enjoyed straight from the bag, added to sandwiches, used as a crunchy layer in salads, or served with low‑salt dips. They are convenient for picnics, road trips, and office snacks.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep chips in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. For longer shelf life, store them in the refrigerator to slow fat oxidation. Discard chips that become soft, develop a stale or rancid smell, or change color.
